```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The window controls how local the trend is and how far it is extrapolated.
Short windows adapt to local movement but estimate the line from less data;
long windows use more observations but impose linearity over a longer span.

```{r}
library(eventsurvey)

dat <- simulate_eventsurvey(seed = 21, pre = 32, post = 9)
windows <- 3:8
fits <- lapply(windows, function(s) {
  eventsurvey(y ~ day, dat, event_time = 0, window = s)
})
sensitivity <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(fits), function(i) {
  cbind(window = windows[i], fits[[i]]$estimate)
}))
sensitivity[, c("window", "effect", "bias_bound", "conf_low", "conf_high")]
```

Changing the window changes the counterfactual, number of rolling exercises,
bias bound, and sampling uncertainty. Interpret them jointly.

Useful prespecified checks include plausible window lengths, including versus
excluding the event period, restrictions motivated by known fieldwork breaks,
and outcomes or subgroups chosen before inspecting results. Do not select the
window that produces the smallest p-value or narrowest interval.
